name: PulseImpute
description: The promise of Mobile Health (mHealth) is the ability to use wearable sensors to monitor participant physiology at high frequencies during daily life to enable temporally-precise health interventions. However, a major challenge is frequent missing data. Despite a rich imputation literature, existing techniques are ineffective for the pulsative signals which comprise many mHealth applications, and a lack of available datasets has stymied progress. We address this gap with PulseImpute, the first large-scale pulsative signal imputation challenge which includes realistic mHealth missingness models, an extensive set of baselines, and clinically-relevant downstream tasks. Our baseline models include a novel transformer-based architecture designed to exploit the structure of pulsative signals. We hope that PulseImpute will enable the ML community to tackle this significant and challenging task.
evaluation_method: MAE/RMSE for imputation, plus downstream task metrics (e.g., classification AUC) for clinical tasks
reputation: A recent research benchmark (PulseImpute) focused on pulsative physiological signal imputation that has attracted interest in the mHealth and time-series communities but is not yet a widely adopted standard.
notes: Non‑LLM benchmark focused on wearable physiological (pulsative) signals; includes realistic missingness models and downstream clinical tasks. Users should note potential dataset size limits, domain-specific signal properties, and that performance varies by downstream task and missingness model.
